text:
maya: Quick note — after the kernel selection change landed yesterday I'm seeing a ~12% P99 latency regression on the replay harness for chat-8k workloads. Need to decide whether this is kernel, batching, or KV cache warmup. anyone have a quick read?

sam: ugh, saw that too. on synthetic load it wasn't as obvious. replay seems to amplify cache misses because of rare long-prefixes. did we change any KV eviction policy?

eli: not eviction, but the kernel change tightened LRU window in the shared cache path. that reduces memory pressure normally but might make warmup worse for rare prefixes.

harper: can we reproduce with a controlled experiment: replay vs synthetic with identical sequence distribution and explicit kv-warmup? i.e. pre-populate the KV cache then run both harnesses.

maya: yes — plan: 1) run replay harness with live traces (baseline), 2) run replay but prewarm KV cache using the first 5% of requests, 3) run synthetic load shaped to match sequence-length and token distribution. compare per-kernel breakdown.

sam: sounds good. small script to prewarm:
```bash
# generate keys from trace and preheat cache
python tools/kv_preheat.py --trace traces/2026-03-14.json --top-percent 5 --target-host runtime-1
```

eli: also please pin batching heuristics for the experiment so we don't conflate dynamic batch shaping. export BATCHER_STRATEGY=static and set batch_size=32 for all runs.

harper: add kernel pin too. last change introduced automatic kernel picker; for apples-to-apples we should force the old kernel and the new kernel separately:
```bash
# force kernel variant
export INFERENCE_KERNEL=fast-matmul-v2
# or
export INFERENCE_KERNEL=quant-dp4a
```

maya: good call. i'll run four configurations: {replay+oldkernel, replay+newkernel, synthetic+oldkernel, synthetic+newkernel} with KV-prewarm on half the runs. will collect token latency histograms and kv-miss rates.

opsbot: deploybot: loadtest cluster provisioned: load-rt-42, 8x A100, replay harness queued. ETA 3m. :rocket:

sam: tiny gotcha — autoscaler can kick during tests and throttle throughput; suggest locking desired instance count to avoid scale events during short runs:
```bash
# lock dedicated pool size
redwoodctl pools update runtime-pool --min 8 --max 8 --policy locked
```

eli: or explicitly measure scale-up separately. we saw 28-35s cold start in last dedicated test when scaling from 0->8. that affects tail latency if burst credits exhausted.

harper: what's the burst-credit model again? i recall each pool accrues credits when underutilized and burns them during spikes. we should include a test where credits = 0 to simulate a drained pool.

maya: yes. adding a step: run the same harness with pool at steady-state (credits full) and after we burn credits by a 30min high-util ramp. that will show graceful degradation vs fallback kernels.

perf-bot: perf-bot: uploaded profile: s3://perf-uploads/1799991111/compare-flamegraphs.html (old vs new kernel). preliminary: new kernel shows 9% higher time in matmul scheduling path and +40% more small-copy syscalls during KV fetch stage.

sam: the syscall spike rings a bell — might be an extra memcpy introduced by the kernel's padding alignment. if true, could explain the P99 shift for long sequences.

eli: can we enable zero-copy KV fetch in the runtime for one run? flag was added last quarter: RUNTIME_KV_ZERO_COPY=true

maya: adding that run too. final matrix: 2 kernels * 3 cache states (cold/no-prewarm, prewarm, zero-copy) * 2 load types (replay, synthetic) = 12 runs. I'll schedule overnight and post results tomorrow morning.

harper: please collect these metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency, tokens/sec, kernel selection distribution, kv-miss-rate, memcpy syscall count, and autoscale events. put raw traces in /mnt/perf/runs/1799991111/

sam: one more: log exact harness command and seed to make runs reproducible. add a small header file with envs and git sha.

maya: will do. SLAs: if new kernel still regresses with zero-copy and prewarm, i'll revert the kernel change for canary and open a bug.

opsbot: deploybot: replay harness started (run id: rh-1799991111-01).

perf-bot: perf-bot: quick diff after first 3 runs: replay+newkernel (cold) P99 = 328ms, replay+oldkernel (cold) P99 = 295ms. KV-miss-rate 13% vs 9%. memcpy count +42%.

maya: ack. thanks everyone. next steps: run full matrix, validate zero-copy impact, check padding in kernel change, and decide canary revert if no improvement. tagging @sam @eli for kernel follow-up. :thumbsup:

sam: i'll dig into kernel padding patch today.

eli: i'll instrument syscall stack for KV fetch to verify where the copies happen.

harper: i'll prepare the autoscale/credits step and lock the pool for the main runs.

maya: thanks — i'll post a short summary with charts when runs finish.
